claim_verdicts.evidence: Design judgement ledgered as opinion. Facts under it hold: three lookups (claims 2, 3), no stage-2 class wraps Keycloak (Program.cs@stage-2 only configures AddJwtBearer with MapInboundClaims = false, RoleClaimType = "roles").

Design judgement with its condition stated ('pays off when that model differs from yours or changes outside your control'). Facts under it: `staff` used as Keycloak spells it (OrderOwnerHandler.cs:22, RoleClaimType = "roles"); the gateway is an outside API the job calls (refund-design.md@stage-2 step 3).
Design judgement phrased as 'where the code runs is a separate decision', not as a rule; the stage-2 fact behind it is claim 11.
Design judgement phrased as a symptom ('You notice this when ...'); rests on the planned design in claim 10.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and too strong. A MimeMessage can be built without From; it is MailKit's SmtpClient (4.18.0) that refuses to send without a sender, taking ResentSender, ResentFrom, Sender, then From (GetMessageSender), else `throw new InvalidOperationException ("No sender has been specified.")`. Same wording in quiz q3 explanation d (en: 'a `MimeMessage` also needs a `From` address'; vi: 'một `MimeMessage` còn cần một địa chỉ `From`').
issues.quote: A `MimeMessage` needs a `From` address, which `IEmailSender` does not name,
issues.fix: §5: 'MailKit will not send a `MimeMessage` without a sender address, and `IEmailSender` names none, so filling `From` with Đơn Hàng's own value is part of the translation.' Ledger it: kind behavior, version_key mailkit, source_hint 'MailKit 4.18.0 SmtpClient.cs GetMessageSender / ValidateArguments: No sender has been specified.' Quiz q3 d en: 'But MailKit will not send a message without a sender address, which `IEmailSender` does not name;' vi: 'Nhưng MailKit không gửi thư thiếu địa chỉ người gửi, mà `IEmailSender` không nhắc tới;'.

issues.text: Direction of the call misdescribed. 'Asks X for Y' means obtaining Y from X; in NotificationSender.cs@stage-2 the job hands the values to IEmailSender: `await email.SendAsync(customer.Email, $"Order {notification.OrderId}: ...`. Same wording in quiz q3 option a (en 'asks `IEmailSender` for'; vi 'chỉ xin `IEmailSender`').
issues.quote: `NotificationSender` asks `IEmailSender` for an address, a subject and a body.
issues.fix: §4: '`NotificationSender` hands `IEmailSender` an address, a subject and a body.' Quiz q3 a en: 'because it hands `IEmailSender` only an address, a subject and a body, never a `MimeMessage`.'; vi: 'vì nó chỉ đưa cho `IEmailSender` một địa chỉ, một tiêu đề và một nội dung, không bao giờ là `MimeMessage`.'

issues.text: Claim 1 (definition, including 'in whichever direction the words cross', which §4 'MailKit is upstream here' and summary line 1 depend on) stays unverified: no DDD source in versions.yaml or refs/. Fact kind, so it does not block.
issues.quote: translates between the upstream model and the downstream one, in whichever direction the words cross
issues.fix: No change to the lesson text. Owner: add a DDD reference under `standards` in content/versions.yaml so claim 1 (and design.l3.conformist claims 1-2) can be checked.

issues.text: The adapter prerequisite told me an adapter 'decides nothing about what to send'. Here the same class fills `From` with Đơn Hàng's own value and that is called part of the translation, and quiz q3 option d ('the old one decides nothing of its own') is marked wrong. The lesson never says how both can be true, so I do not know which statement to keep.
issues.quote: so filling it with Đơn Hàng's own value is part of the translation.
issues.fix: Add one sentence right after it: 'This does not contradict the adapter lesson: address, subject and body still come from the caller; `From` is one fixed Đơn Hàng value, the same for every email, that `IEmailSender` leaves out.'

issues.text: I know upstream and downstream as bounded contexts, each with its own model. MailKit is a library, and this is the first time a library is treated as an upstream context. The 'since' clause helps, but I paused to accept that a library has a model in the same sense.
issues.quote: MailKit is upstream here, since Đơn Hàng must follow its model to send mail.
issues.fix: Add one clause after 'to send mail': ', and a library has a model too: its own types, names and rules'.

issues.text: This is given as the reason to translate, but at this point nothing has shown me why a Keycloak user differs from a customer. Section 5 later shows the evidence (two different ids; a caller with no customer row), so reading in order I had to take it on trust.
issues.quote: A Keycloak user is not a customer, so Đơn Hàng translates the user;
issues.fix: Add the reason in parentheses after 'not a customer': '(its `sub` is not a customer id, and a staff user has no customer row at all)'.

issues.text: Core concepts and section 4 say translation covers 'words, values and rules', but no example is labelled as a word, a value or a rule. I can match the rules (no customer row means no owner; the 24-hour limit) but not which example is a 'value', so I cannot use the three-way split on a new case.
issues.quote: Adapter is one tool for such a layer, whose job is wider: words, values and rules.
issues.fix: After 'words, values and rules', add one sentence labelling one example of each: word, `sub` becoming a `Customer`; value, the gateway's status text becoming `refunded` or `failed`; rule, the 24-hour limit.

issues.text: I can narrate every node and arrow, but the diagram marks no edge: in the top row the layer is an arrow (the lookup), in the middle row it is a node (`MailKitEmailSender`), in the bottom row it is an arrow label. I had to work out from the prose which part of each row is the layer.
issues.quote: These lookups are the anti-corruption layer toward Keycloak.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before the top-row paragraph: 'In each row, the layer is the step between the outside word and Đơn Hàng's word: the lookup arrow on top, `MailKitEmailSender` in the middle, the refund job at the bottom.'

issues.text: I re-read this sentence twice: the colon, then a rule embedded between commas, then 'not only a name' at the end, which seems to attach to the rule rather than to 'carries'.
issues.quote: A caller without the `staff` role and with no customer row ends as `null` and never meets the requirement: the translation carries a rule, Đơn Hàng's rule that a Keycloak user with no customer row owns no order, not only a name.
issues.fix: Split it: '... ends as `null` and never meets the requirement. So the translation carries a rule, not only a name: a Keycloak user with no customer row owns no order.'

issues.text: Option b assumes the other library also needs a sender address. The lesson only tells me a `MimeMessage` needs `From`; nothing says another library's message does. I picked b because any email seems to need a sender, which is knowledge from outside the lesson.
issues.quote: The new class must also decide the `From` address, because today that choice is made inside `MailKitEmailSender`.
issues.fix: Add one sentence to the q3 stem (en and vi): 'Like MailKit, the other library sends no message without a sender address.'
